description: fz has no bit_size/1: a call reports lower/unbound. Macro.escape (fz-sc8.225) needs it to escape a bitstring that is not a binary (the first rem(bit_size, 8) bits as an integer, then the rest as a binary). The runtime already knows the bit length (fz_bitstring_byte_extent reads it to round up). Add a Kernel function backed by a runtime export that answers the bit length; a non-bitstring raises Elixir's ArgumentError '1st argument: not a bitstring', as byte_size does. Done when: an oracle fixture (oracle: self) shows bit_size of <<>>, <<1::3>>, <<1, 2::4>>, a binary, and the raise, on interp, run and build. Proposal: https://claude.ai/artifact/N14ZzKaX8vUSfrX4Uxx58t (ticket A).
title: bit_size/1 answers how many bits a bitstring has, as in Elixir
